processing: Ripe pu-erh using larger, lower-grade leaf (grade 9 by one account), often with a fair share of stems collected at the factory, pressed into cakes.
harvest_season: Not tied to one picking: it is a blend of fermented leaf and stems.
appearance_dry: A 357 g dark brown cake of coarse large leaf with plenty of visible stems.
appearance_wet: Large soft dark leaves mixed with stems.
taste_profile: Woody with an aged aroma, and light on bitterness or depth compared with finer blends, as is typical of stem-rich ripe tea.

brewing.notes: Coarse leaf and stems take time to give flavour, so steep a little longer than for a fine ripe tea. Boiling water suits it.

vintage_note: Sold by year and batch, usually as 357 g cakes, with reviewed examples including batch 1601 and a 2023 pressing. It is a budget recipe rather than a collector piece, so buy it for daily drinking. Storage still mellows it.
description:
7592 is the plain sibling of the famous 7572, a Menghai Tea Factory ripe cake that is meant to be drunk rather than collected. By one seller's account it was designed in 1975 as a cheaper alternative, with larger leaf at a lower grade.

The leaf is coarse, and it is said to be grade 9 on average. A collector's account adds that the factory took to gathering its stems each year for this recipe, so expect to see a good many in the cake.

The cup is a bright, clear red with wood and an aged aroma. Compared with finer ripe teas it will seem lighter in depth, which is the usual effect of larger leaf and stems. It takes boiling water and longer steeps well.

Do not take stems as a flaw here; they belong in this recipe. Buy by batch and compare it with 7572 if you want to learn what grade does to a ripe tea.
history:
A seller dates the recipe to 1975 at the Menghai factory, as an economical counterpart to 7572; no factory record of that date is at hand. Yunnan's provincial tea company is said to have introduced a unified export numbering system in 1976.

A collector's account says stems collected at the factory became a regular part of 7592 production. Batches are still being made, as a 2023 pressing shows.
